title: A Nushell filter, Recents and search results keep an old answer when a file changes but the list of paths does not
problem:
Found by the review of the whole branch (20 Nov), in which one reviewer read all the improvements together through one lens and a second reviewer tried to refute each finding against the code. Nothing was run in that review: every finding was traced by reading. [filter-answer-kept-while-paths-are-the-same] A Nushell filter is run again only when the list of paths changes: saved files, folder sizes that arrive later, Refresh and Return leave its old answer in force. The finder's scenario: Needs nu. A folder sorted by name with a.log (5 KB) and b.log (50 KB). Filter bar: `size > 10kb`; b.log shows. Another program saves a.log at 80 KB (draft renamed over it). After the two-second look the folder is read again and the rows have the new sizes, but a.log stays hidden. Save b.log at 1 KB the same way: it stays listed, showing 1 KB under `size > 10kb`, and the status bar goes on counting it as passing. Cmd+R changes nothing, and neither does Return in the filter field (`set_filter` returns when the text is the same); only editing the filter's text runs it again. With one file in the folder, "No Items Pass the Filter. 1 item is hidden by the filter." stays up after the file has grown past the limit. Second case, by reading: with folder sizes on, the first run after opening a folder judges the folders before `load_folder_stats` has filled their sizes in; when the sizes arrive the rows show them and the filter is not run again, so `size > 100mb` never lists a big folder in a folder opened with the filter on. What should happen: the filter runs again when what it is given for a row (size, date) changed, and at the least on Refresh. Origin: the path-only comparison is upstream's (66c919b had the same `apply_filter_to`); the branch added the message that states the count and the promise that rows and previews follow saved files, which the filter beside them now contradicts. The code path: src/finder/filter.rs:130-138 (`filter_source` is the ordered list of paths; a run starts only when it differs, otherwise `filter_keep` is applied as it is). filter.rs:83-100 (`set_filter` returns for the same text; it and src/finder/mod.rs:3699-3705 `nu_changed` are the only places that forget the answer). mod.rs:1757-1765 (`refresh` resets nothing of the filter). mod.rs:1835-1836 (`rebuild_rows` -> `apply_filter_to`). src/nushell.rs:69-84 (the filter is given each row's size and modified). src/finder/list.rs:153-156 and 177-183 (folder sizes are filled in later, then `rebuild_rows` with the same paths). mod.rs:4820-4834 and src/finder/bars.rs:353-366 (the message and the status count go by the old answer). The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: As the finder says, with these limits. The saved-file and Refresh cases need the rows' paths and order to stay the same: a sort by name does that, while Sort By Size (or by date for a date filter) moves the changed row and the filter runs again. A visible draft that a 2-second look happens to catch in the folder also makes it run again. The folder case exactly: type `size > 100mb` in a folder whose sizes have loaded and its big folders are listed; open another folder with the filter still on and that folder's big folders are not listed, until the folder gains or loses an item (the reread then finds the stats still in the map and the paths changed, so the filter runs with sizes). With Sort By Size the arrival of the sizes reorders the folders and the filter runs again by itself. Their evidence: src/finder/filter.rs:130-138: `let paths: Vec<PathBuf> = rows.iter().map(|r| r.entry.path.clone()).collect(); if self.filter_source.as_ref() != Some(&paths) { self.filter_source = Some(paths); let entries ...; self.start_filter(entries, cx); } if let Some(keep) = &self.filter_keep { rows.retain(|r| keep.contains(&r.entry.path)); }`. A run starts only when the ordered list of paths differs. `filter_source` is reset in two places only (grep over src): `set_filter` (filter.rs:90-91), which is behind `if text == self.filter { return; }` at 85-87, so Return with the same text does nothing; and `nu_changed` (mod.rs:3700-3701). `refresh` (mod.rs:1757-1765) clears the previews and reloads, and touches nothing of the filter. The status count is `self.rows.len()` after that keep-set (src/finder/bars.rs:351-366).

Folder sizes: `location_changed` empties `folder_stats` (mod.rs:1300). `load_listing`'s completion starts `load_folder_stats` (async) and calls `rebuild_rows` in the same update (mod.rs:1533, 1545), so `decorate` (src/finder/list.rs:177-181) finds no stats and the first run is given `"size": null` for every folder (src/nushell.rs:78). When the stats arrive only `rebuild_rows` runs (list.rs:153-156): same paths, no run. Checked with the installed nu 0.116.0 on inline sample rows in the filter's own pipeline shape: a row with size null is dropped by `where size > 100mb`, with no error. `folder_sizes` is on by default (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:308).

No test changes a row's size or presses Refresh under a filter. Not in any done record or in final-pass-notes.md: filter-stale-keep-set is about a keep-set applied to another place's rows. Origin: upstream's and unchanged by the branch (`git show 66c919b:src/finder/filter.rs` has the same comparison; the 2-second folder reread and `load_folder_stats` are upstream's too). Not run in the window. [listed-file-saved-keeps-old-row-and-preview] A file saved the usual way keeps its old size, date and preview in Recents (when it stays where it was) and in name-search results: the reread's answer is compared by path only and dropped. The finder's scenario: 1. Recents (Cmd+Shift+F), Preview Pane on (Cmd+Shift+P). The newest file, say notes.txt, is first: select it. 2. Save notes.txt again from an editor that writes a draft and renames it over the file (most do). It is still the newest, so it stays first. 3. Wait. What happens: the row keeps the old Date Modified and Size and the pane (Quick Look and the gallery too) keeps the old text, for good. The index reported the rename, the window read Recents again and the answer held the new size and date, but `fresh` only asks whether the paths differ, so the answer is thrown away, `listing` is not replaced and `selection_changed` is never reached. The same save seen in the file's own folder updates row and preview within two seconds. In the results of a search by name it is the same for any listed file: a file the search already lists is no news to `changes_for`, and when a rerun does happen (the draft's name had the words) `Stale::shows_in` compares paths, so `results` keeps the old entries. What should happen: the row shows the new size and date and the preview is read again, as docs/manual.md:424 says ("...when a search runs again, or when Recents is read again. Most programs save a file under another name that then takes the file's ... so the preview follows within a couple of seconds") and as both changes' changelog entries say. Already recorded, and not what this is about: files written over in place (final-pass-notes lines 47 and 71, manual line 139 "with the size and date it showed"). Not recorded: the ordinary save by rename, and that Recents reads the newer rows and drops them. The code path: src/finder/mod.rs:1647-1670 (Recents look: a rename is news, so `reload_recents` runs) -> mod.rs:1675-1699 (`fresh` = the paths differ, 1685-1689; `listing` replaced and `selection_changed` called only `if fresh`, 1691-1696). Name search: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:762-776 (a file that came matters only when `!lists(now)`) and src/finder/mod.rs:2273-2284 (`fresh` from `Stale::shows_in`; `if !fresh { return retry; }` before `results` is written) with mod.rs:356-369 (`shows_in` compares paths). engine.rs:1316-1325 (`recents` hands back the index's size and date). src/finder/preview.rs:329-331 and 338-348 (the stamp is the row's entry, so a row that isn't replaced never asks again). The second reviewer, who tried to refute it and confirmed it, corrects the scenario: The row and the preview stay as they were until Recents next comes out as another list, the search's rows change, or Cmd+R; not for good. How it happens depends on what the watcher reports. A draft made and renamed within one batch reaches the app as `Modified` of the target: fff-notify-debouncer-full-0.9.4 src/lib.rs:469-484 rewrites the draft's events to the target path and adds no rename event "unless the file was just created", and fff-search-0.11.0 src/watcher/background_watcher.rs:629-632 gives `None if existed => (WatchEventKind::Modified, None)`. Then for the first file in Recents `only_written_since` names it and nothing is read at all (mod.rs:1659-1664: `if news || written.as_deref() != first { fell_behind }`), which is the documented skip, and a name search hears nothing (Modified counts only in `recent`, engine.rs:396-409). Recents is read and its answer dropped, as the finder describes, only when the save arrives as Renamed or Created: a draft that outlived a batch, or an editor that moves the old file aside first. A listed file never makes a name search run again in either case. The finder's fix (take the answer when stamps differ) reaches only the read-and-dropped case, not the usual quick save. Their evidence: The outcome is real, and nothing guards against it. Recents: src/finder/mod.rs:1685-1696 `let fresh = !this.listing.iter().map(|entry| &entry.path).eq(entries.iter().map(|entry| &entry.path)); this.recents_behind.caught_up(fresh); if fresh { this.listing = entries; this.rebuild_rows(cx); this.selection_changed(cx); }`: an answer with the same paths in the same order is dropped with its new sizes and dates. Name search: crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:770-775 `if let Some((now, lower)) = now && may_list(now, lower) && !lists(now) { matter.push(now.clone()); }` (a listed file is no news; the draft in `was` is not listed and left no folder, 763-768), and mod.rs:2274-2284 `let fresh = partial || stale.as_ref().is_none_or(|stale| stale.shows_in(&this.results, &rows)); ... if !fresh { return retry; }`, with `shows_in` comparing paths only (356-369). The preview goes by the row: src/finder/preview.rs:329-331 `(entry.modified, entry.size.filter(|_| !entry.is_dir))` and 346-348 `if current == Some(&stamp) { return; }`. Refresh (mod.rs:1757-1762) reads both lists again.

It is recorded as known and left, and tests pin it. done/live-search-results.json: behaviour_changes "While it is first, further writes read nothing and its row keeps the size and date it showed"; left_out "Rows of files changed in place keep their old size and date until the list is next replaced ... That includes a file that stays first in Recents"; notes "`reload_recents` shows a list only when its paths or their order differ" and "a quiet rerun compares which paths are listed, not their sizes or dates ... a preview cache stamped from the row won't see a new stamp from it". done/stale-previews-and-cancel.json, Found, not fixed: "In the results of a search by name a file changed in place keeps the index's size and date, so its preview isn't read again until the search's rows change". final-pass-notes.md lines 47 and 71. docs/manual.md:139 says of Recents "stays there however often it's written to, with the size and date it showed". tests/finder.rs:1126-1133 pins "stays first, so Recents isn't read again"; engine.rs:3662 pins "a file the search lists already is nothing new to it". So the finder's "not recorded: that Recents reads the newer rows and drops them" is wrong: it is in the done record's notes. The finder's quote of manual.md:424 also leaves out "which changes the folder": that sentence promises the couple of seconds for folders only.

What the records do not say in so many words: in these two lists a save by rename is treated no differently from a write in place. "Changed in place" in final-pass-notes 47 and 71 therefore understates the limit: any save of a file that stays listed (name search) or stays first (Recents) leaves its row and preview as they were.
proposal: Reproduce each fault first with a test that fails on the trunk. Then fix it. The finder's suggested fixes, as starting points and not checked plans: [filter-answer-kept-while-paths-are-the-same] Keep in `filter_source` what the filter is given for each row, (path, size, modified), and compare that in `apply_filter_to`; and set `filter_source = None` in `refresh`. [listed-file-saved-keeps-old-row-and-preview] In `reload_recents`, also take the answer when the paths are the same in the same order but some entry's (modified, size) differs: replace `listing`, `rebuild_rows`, `selection_changed`, and count it as fresh (the order is the same, so nothing reshuffles). In the quiet search's answer, when it is not fresh but `paths_of(&this.results).eq(paths_of(&rows))`, take `rows` and call `selection_changed` instead of returning.
original_test_plan: The finder's test ideas: [filter-answer-kept-while-paths-are-the-same] Where nu is installed (return early otherwise, as the other filter tests do): a fixture folder with small.txt of 1 byte, `set_filter("size > 10b")`, assert small.txt is not listed. Write 100 bytes to a draft and rename it over small.txt, `ui.look_for_changes(1)`, assert small.txt is listed. Fails today. A second block: write over a file in place, `ui.press(&cmd("r"))`, same assertion. [listed-file-saved-keeps-old-row-and-preview] tests/finder.rs: Recents with Roadmap.md the newest and selected, Preview Pane on. Write new text to a draft and rename it over Roadmap.md, `ui.reindex()`, `ui.report_change(Some(&draft), Some(&roadmap))` (a rename), `ui.look_for_changes(2)`. Assert `preview_text_for_test(&roadmap)` is the new text and the row's size label is the new one. Today both are the old ones. The same with a search for `roadmap` in place of Recents. Why the existing tests miss it: [filter-answer-kept-while-paths-are-the-same] The filter tests change the filter's text or the set of rows. None changes a row's size or date while a filter is on, and none presses Refresh under a filter. what_waited_for_a_nu_runs_with_the_one_chosen_in_settings covers only a change of `nu`. [listed-file-saved-keeps-old-row-and-preview] tests/finder.rs:1164-1188 (recents_previews_a_file_as_it_was_last_written) writes to the second file so that it moves first, which changes the order and so counts as fresh. tests/finder.rs:1126-1136 pins "stays first, so Recents isn't read again" and looks at names only. No test saves a listed file that keeps its place and then looks at its row or its preview, in Recents or in a search.
original_risks: This is a fix late in the branch: keep it to the fault. Every test on the trunk has to keep passing, and the improvements involved (empty-state-messages, live-search-results, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, stale-previews-and-cancel) have tests that pin the behaviour around the fault: read their done records in /home/user/polish-tools/done/ before changing the functions they changed.

verifier.claim_check: A second reviewer traced the same path and confirmed it; neither ran anything. Reproduce before changing anything; if a test shows the fault is not there, write the closed record with the evidence and return skipped.

orchestrator_notes: This fault was in the app before this branch, at least in part: write a normal `Changelog (Fixed):` paragraph for what a user of the last release would notice. The full findings, with the second reviewer's evidence line by line, are in /home/user/polish-tools/review/*.md and *.json (search for the finding ids in brackets). The review read the branch at 7e8df53; other changes have landed since, so read the functions as they are now. Two faults with one cause: an answer is compared with what is on screen by paths alone. The filter half was so before the branch (write the Changelog paragraph for it). The Recents and quiet-rerun half is in 'live-search-results' (153eb8f) and 'stale-previews-and-cancel' (52e7de4), both unreleased, and needs no changelog sentence of its own. 'filter-stale-keep-set' is a saved-for-later item about a different fault in the same function (the last answer applied to another place's rows): do not take it on, and do not make it worse. The filter tests need nu (/usr/local/bin/nu here); follow tests/controls.rs for how they skip without it. 'empty-state-messages' (f60d2e4) pinned when the message and the placeholders show while a filter runs: a filter that now runs again more often must not make the list flicker on every two-second look, so run it again only when a row's size or date really changed.
